label: input u at late original positions (6-8)
explanation: Fires only when the input token is the letter u at original position 6, 7 or 8 (orig_idx >= 6). It never fires on u at positions 0-5, on any other token, or at the delimiter or copy steps. Magnitude rises with position: u at positions 7-8 always fires and is strong (around 0.4-1.0 of max; 94% of mass). u at position 6 fires only about 45% of the time and weakly (<0.15 of max; about 6% of mass). Whether u at position 6 fires does not depend on L, prev_tok or n_digits; it is only slightly more likely when this is the first u in the sequence (49% vs 29%). The strongest activations are u at position 8, the last original token of length-9 sequences. Predicate u & orig_idx>=7 gives precision 1.0 and mass recall 0.94.

issues: The test scores reproduce: precision 0.726, recall 1.0, F1 0.841, mass recall 1.0. Misses with --split test found 0 missed activations.

Every false positive is u at original position 6 (4539 test steps). That matches the explanation's position-6 caveat. Position 6 holds only 5.8% of the activation mass. Positions 7 and 8 hold 49% and 45%.

Whether u at position 6 fires is not explained by any simple variable. Precision there is 0.45 for each of L = 7, 8 and 9, about 0.45 to 0.47 across n_digits, 0.49 for a first u versus 0.29 for a repeat u, and between 0.30 and 0.53 depending on prev_tok (e.g. e 0.30, k 0.53). Checks of which tokens appeared earlier (seen a/e/q/z/0) gave 0.36 to 0.56. This is spread-out dependence on history, not a rule. The claim that prev_tok has no effect is slightly overstated, but no clean subclass exists.
Alternative predicate u & orig_idx >= 7: test precision 1.0, recall 0.70, mass recall 0.944, F1 0.821. That is lower F1 than the recorded predicate, so it is not better.
The profile confirms zero activation in the delimiter and copy phases, at positions 0-5, and on every token other than u. Mean magnitude rises with position.
